'''Mark Brian Wise''' (November 9, 1953 – July 10, 2026) was a Canadian-American theoretical physicist. He conducted research in [[elementary particles|elementary particle physics]] and [[physical cosmology|cosmology]].<ref name="amacad">{{cite web |date=July 2026 |title=Mark Brian Wise |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/mark-brian-wise |website=Member Directory |location=Cambridge, MA |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref> He is best known for his role in the development of [[heavy quark effective theory]] (HQET), a mathematical formalism that has allowed physicists to make predictions about otherwise intractable problems in the [[Quantum chromodynamics|theory of the strong nuclear interactions]]. He also published work on mathematical models for [[finance]] and [[risk assessment]].

== Early life and education ==
Wise was born in [[Montreal]] on November 9, 1953.  From the age of four he grew up in [[Toronto]].<ref name="aip-oral">{{cite web |last=Zierler |first=David |date=18 February 2021 |title=Wise, Mark |url=https://repository.aip.org/node/129576 |website=Oral History Interviews (OHI) |location=College Park, MD |publisher=American Institute of Physics |access-date=}}</ref> He was educated at the [[University of Toronto]] ([[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]], 1976; [[Master of Science|M.S.]], 1977) before moving to the USA to attend [[Stanford University]] ([[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]], 1980). While still a student, he co-authored a book on mathematical methods in physics with Toronto professor Lynn Trainor.

== Academic career ==
With [[Fred Gilman]], his graduate advisor at Stanford, Wise wrote several highly influential papers on experimental predictions of the [[quark]] model.  He was a junior fellow at the [[Harvard Society of Fellows]] from 1980 to 1983, and then became an assistant professor at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech).<ref name="CIT-obit">{{cite web|url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-mourns-the-passing-of-mark-b-wise-19532026 |title=Caltech Mourns the Passing of Mark B. Wise (1953–2026) |website=Caltech News |publisher=Caltech |access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref>  He was promoted to associate professor in 1984 and to full professor in 1985.<ref name="CIT-obit" />  From 1984 to 1987 he was a fellow of the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref name="aip-oral" />

In 1992 he was appointed [[John McCone|John A. McCone]] Professor of High Energy Physics at Caltech, a position that he held until his death in 2026.<ref name="CIT-obit" />  As a professor at Caltech, Wise supervised over three dozen doctoral students in theoretical physics.<ref name="physicstree">{{Cite web|title=Physics Tree – Mark B. Wise |url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=125278 |access-date=2021-03-07 |website=academictree.org}}</ref>

== Other pursuits ==
Wise worked as consultant for [[PIMCO]], an [[investment management]] firm specializing in [[fixed income]].  He collaborated with PIMCO's Vineer Bhansali and the two co-authored a textbook on fixed income finance, published by [[McGraw Hill Education|McGraw Hill]] in 2010.  Wise regarded his work on mathematical finance and his own personal investing as a "hobby".<ref name="aip-oral" />  He also acted as science consultant for the movie ''[[Iron Man 2]]'' (2010).<ref name="ironman">{{cite web |last=Lorditch |first=Emilie |date=May 5, 2010 |title=Inside Science Of Iron Man 2 |url=https://www.aip.org/inside-science/inside-science-of-iron-man-2 |website=Inside Science |location=College Park, MD |publisher=American Institute of Physics |access-date=23 July 2026}}</ref>

== Honors ==
Wise shared the 2001 [[Sakurai Prize]] for Theoretical Particle Physics with [[Nathan Isgur]] and [[Mikhail Voloshin]], "for the construction of the heavy [[quark]] mass expansion and the discovery of the heavy quark symmetry in [[quantum chromodynamics]], which led to a quantitative theory of the decays of ''c'' and ''b'' flavored [[hadron]]s."<ref name="sakurai-prize">{{Cite web|title=Caltech Physicist Awarded Sakurai Prize |url=https://www.caltech.edu/about/news/caltech-physicist-awarded-sakurai-prize-466 |access-date=2021-03-07 |website=California Institute of Technology |date=April 2, 2001 |language=en}}</ref>  He was elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2002,<ref name="amacad" /> fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2003,<ref name="aps">{{cite web |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |title=APS Fellow Archive |publisher=APS |access-date=17 September 2020}}</ref> and member of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2007.<ref name="NAS">{{Cite web|title=Mark Wise|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/mark-b-wise-hnlhjq/ |access-date=2021-03-07|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>  In 2021 he received the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]]'s [[Julius Wess]] Award for "his outstanding and groundbreaking scientific achievements in the field of theoretical particle physics, in particular the development of modern effective field theories for flavor physics, and his high international reputation."<ref name="Wess-award">{{Cite web|title=Mark Wise erhält Julius Wess-Preis 2021 |url=https://www.kit.edu/kit/pi_2021_096_mark-wise-erhalt-julius-wess-preis-2021.php |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Karlsruhe Institüt fur Technologie |date=October 28, 2021 |language=de}}</ref> 

== Death ==
Wise died on July 10, 2026, at the age of 72.<ref name="CIT-obit" />  His friend and colleague at Caltech, [[John Preskill]], eulogized him as "one of the most influential figures in theoretical particle physics of his generation."<ref name="Preskill-memorial">{{cite web |last=Preskill |first=John |date=July 18, 2026 |title=My friend Mark Wise |url=https://quantumfrontiers.com/2026/07/18/my-friend-mark-wise/ |website=Quantum Frontiers |location=Pasadena, CA |publisher=Institute for Quantum Information and Matter |access-date=July 25, 2026 |author-link=John Preskill}}</ref>
